parent: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles N.V. (Stellantis N.V. from Jan 2021)
notes: FCA N.V. 20-F for 2019 reports 191,752 employees, incorporated in the Netherlands with principal executive offices in London. FCA US LLC (Toledo Jeep plants) became a Stellantis N.V. (Netherlands) subsidiary on Jan 16, 2021, which covers the FY2021 grant.

parent: Port of Greater Cincinnati Development Authority
notes: Public port authority created by the City of Cincinnati and Hamilton County; grants were Revitalization and OSIP spec-development money passed through to sites. Staff is a few dozen per its website and audited financial report; no exact headcount was published.

JSW Steel USA Ohio is the former Acero Junction mill in Mingo Junction, bought in 2018 by JSW Steel Ltd of Mumbai (JSW Group), which reported well over 10,000 employees through the grant years. Form 5500 shows 333 to 345 participants at the Ohio entity alone; JobsOhio counted 400 retained jobs.

North Star BlueScope Steel in Delta became wholly owned by Melbourne-based BlueScope Steel after it bought Cargill's 50 percent in 2015; BlueScope reported roughly 14,000 employees in FY2020 and 16,500 in 2024. Form 5500 shows 477 to 656 participants at the Delta mill alone.

Silfex is a wholly owned subsidiary of Lam Research (Fremont, CA), whose FY2019 10-K reports approximately 10,700 regular employees. Silfex has operated in Eaton since 1971 and expanded into Springfield, but the parent is Californian.

Privately held, woman-owned silicone maker with a single 200,000 sq ft Cleveland site; JobsOhio counted 113 retained jobs and 50 new jobs tied to the R&D Center Grant, and the company cites 45 percent workforce growth from 2018 to 2022. No exact total headcount was published, but one site with roughly 113 to 170 jobs puts it in 100-499.

County economic development port authority that received a $3.09 million JobsOhio spec-development (OSIP) grant to buy and prepare the National Road Business Park site. It is a small public agency with a handful of staff; no headcount is published.

Libbey's last 10-K (2019) reports 5,872 employees, about 70 percent outside the US; the company went through Chapter 11 in 2020 and emerged privately held by its former lenders as Libbey Glass LLC, still headquartered in Toledo. Founded in 1818 in Massachusetts and moved to Toledo in 1888; Form 5500 shows 2,349 US participants in 2023, so post-bankruptcy worldwide headcount near 5,000 is an estimate.

Family-owned Purell maker founded in Akron in 1946 and headquartered there; Wooster is a plant. Roughly 2,500 employees, consistent with Form 5500 participant counts of 2,086 (2019) and 2,373 (2023); Clorox agreed to buy GOJO in January 2026, after the grant years.

parent: Pratt Industries, Inc. (Anthony Pratt / Visy group)
notes: Pratt Paper (OH) LLC is the Wapakoneta recycled-paper mill of Pratt Industries, the Conyers, Georgia US arm of Anthony Pratt's privately held Visy group of Melbourne, Australia; the combined group reported about 11,000 employees in 2020. Pratt Industries alone does not publish a headcount, but with six mills and dozens of plants it is well above 5,000.

Paycor's first 10-K (FY ended June 30, 2021) reports 2,067 associates and Cincinnati headquarters; Form 5500 shows 2,069 participants in 2019. During the FY2020 grant Paycor was majority owned by private equity firm Apax Partners (acquired Nov 2018), and it went public in July 2021.

Breeze Airways, founded by David Neeleman in 2018 and based in Cottonwood Heights, Utah, began flying in May 2021; Form 5500 shows 1,025 plan participants in 2023 and the airline reports about 2,262 employees in 2026. The grants are JobsOhio Air Service Restoration payments for routes at Akron-Canton, not a plant or office project.

Privately held glove startup founded in Grove City in 2021 by Jacob Block, financed with $105 million from Orion Infrastructure Capital, and the first pre-revenue company to get a JobsOhio grant ($3.5 million committed). It planned 400 jobs, but Form 5500 shows only 33 plan participants in 2023, so actual headcount in the grant years may have been under 100.

Nestle USA (Solon R&D and headquarters functions) is a subsidiary of Nestlé S.A. of Vevey, Switzerland, which reported 291,000 employees in 2019 and 276,000 in 2021. Form 5500 shows over 44,000 US plan participants.

Seefried is a privately held Atlanta industrial developer (founded 1984 by Ferdinand Seefried) with roughly 58 employees per LinkedIn; it built Amazon's Ohio fulfillment centers, including the Akron Rolling Acres site named in JobsOhio's 2019 release. The FY2021 grant is site money for an Amazon building, so the beneficiary tenant was Amazon, not a small company.

Municipal government; grants were an Aerospace and Defense Opportunity Grant and OSIP money for the National Advanced Air Mobility Center of Excellence and related infrastructure at Springfield-Beckley Municipal Airport. City workforce is in the several hundreds, but no published headcount was found on the city site or in JobsOhio materials.

Altivia Petrochemicals is a unit of privately owned ALTIVIA of Houston (founded 1986), which bought the Haverhill phenol plant in 2015; JobsOhio counted 137 retained jobs there and LinkedIn lists about 220 employees company-wide. Form 5500 shows 418 participants at the petrochemicals unit in 2023, so total headcount across ALTIVIA's seven units could be near 500.

Privately held freight brokerage founded in Cincinnati in 1997 by Ken Oaks and headquartered in Union Township, Clermont County; JobsOhio's 2022 release puts headcount over 9,000 after 49 percent growth in 2021, implying roughly 6,000 in 2020. JobsOhio counted 2,623 retained Ohio jobs.

Medpace's 2019 10-K reports approximately 3,500 employees worldwide and Cincinnati headquarters; founded there in 1992 by August Troendle. Form 5500 shows 2,189 participants in 2019 and 3,462 in 2023, and JobsOhio counted 1,916 retained Ohio jobs.

Dana Limited is a subsidiary of Dana Incorporated (NYSE: DAN), headquartered in Maumee, whose 2018 10-K reports approximately 30,900 employees. The 10-K traces the business to 1904 but does not name the founding city.
